programme: No single module unites these twelve factors. They fall into at least four unrelated axes: NFE2-driven heme/globin synthesis (HBB, ALAS2, AHSP, HBD, ANK1, GCM1, HMBS — a classic erythroid-maturation signature); ATF6B unfolded-protein-response signaling; a stress/ubiquitin cluster of HIPK2 (p53-linked stress kinase) and RBCK1 (LUBAC component, NF-kB-linked linear ubiquitination); an interferon-stimulated-gene trio of STAT2, TRIM22 and SP100; and a scattering of unrelated regulators — NCOA2 (nuclear receptor coactivation), TGIF1 (TGF-beta/SMAD corepression), BATF (AP-1, Th17 differentiation), KLF4 (broad epithelial/vascular TF) and ZNF461 (uncharacterized). None of these axes share a target, complex, or pathway with another in the list.
role_in_a: Not established — no coherent module can be assigned a role in cardiovascular disease from this factor set.
role_in_b: Not established — no coherent module can be assigned a role in fibromyalgia from this factor set.
shared_axis: No shared mechanism can be proposed. The only internally consistent sub-cluster, STAT2/TRIM22/SP100 as interferon-stimulated genes, is also the weakest by recurrence (15/32) and its natural upstream partner STAT1 was excluded as tissue-generic in blood, meaning any interferon story here would just be restating ordinary blood immune activity rather than a disease-specific link.
reasoning: The four most-recurring factors (ATF6B 21/32, HIPK2 21/32, NFE2 20/32, RBCK1 20/32) sit in four different pathways — UPR, p53/stress kinase, erythroid transcription, and LUBAC ubiquitination — with no known cross-talk connecting them, so the strongest signal in the data does not point to a mechanism. No factor carries an Open Targets association with either disease, and every retrieved paper is either absent or judged by the reader as not clearly addressing the disease in question, so there is nothing in the record to anchor a story to.
support: PMID 28275299 (HIPK2): about gastric cancer, does not mention fibromyalgia — does not support the claim. PMID 35204312 (NFE2/Nrf2): peripheral neuropathic pain models, fibromyalgia relevance unclear — does not support the claim. PMID 38632385 (KLF4): neonatal monocyte inflammation, no fibromyalgia reference shown — does not support the claim.
how_to_falsify: Take blood samples (or public expression/ChIP data) from cardiovascular-disease and fibromyalgia cohorts and test whether ATF6B, HIPK2, NFE2 and RBCK1 converge on any shared target gene set or pathway (e.g. joint pathway enrichment on their combined target lists, or co-occupancy at shared promoters/enhancers by ChIP-seq). If they show no common downstream targets or co-regulatory relationship, the 'no coherent module' call is confirmed; if a shared regulatory circuit or physical interaction is found linking, say, HIPK2 and RBCK1 to NFE2-driven erythroid/heme genes, the incoherent verdict should be revised.
caveats: Tissue pairing is blood|blood, but the 32 patient-group comparisons come from only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the recurrence counts reflect within-cohort subgrouping rather than 32 independent replications. The tissue-generic exclusion list removes STAT1, IRF8, CEBPB, RELB and other interferon/myeloid regulators as ordinary for blood, which undercuts building any story around the surviving interferon-pathway members (STAT2, TRIM22, SP100) as disease-specific. The single-view exclusions (e.g. FOXP2, SIRT6, CBFA2T3) removed factors that were individually more disease-plausible but did not recur, which is the reason this account does not reach for them.
